title: ECOLINK
card_summary: A barangay reporting system where residents report problems with a live photo and map pin, and staff resolve them under deadlines.
overview: ECOLINK is a reporting system for Barangay Santo Cristo. Residents report community problems with a live photo and an exact map location. Barangay staff sort and resolve reports from one queue under deadlines, and residents get updates by SMS. I designed, built and deployed the whole system while my 3 groupmates wrote the capstone paper.
features: Role-based access for 5 roles, checked on every request
A deadline on every report, with a job every 5 minutes that escalates, cancels or warns on late ones
4 layers against fake reports: SMS OTP with ID approval, camera-only photos with a date check, a geofence and account blocking
Automatic routing of reports to barangay departments
Online requests for 6 barangay documents with reference numbers, status tracking and an audit log
Real-time admin alerts and SMS status updates

decisions.a: Notifications only go one way, from the server to the browser, so SSE is simpler and reconnects by itself.

decisions.q: Flag suspicious photos instead of rejecting them
decisions.a: Some phones remove photo data, so a real report could get blocked. A staff member makes the final call.

decisions.q: Disable categories instead of deleting them
decisions.a: Old reports keep their original labels, so the records stay accurate.

decisions.q: Move from Google Cloud to free hosting
decisions.a: I first deployed with Docker on Google Cloud Run. When the free trial ended, I moved the database to Aiven MySQL, the photos to Supabase Storage and the app to Render, updated the saved photo links, and set up regular database backups.

title: TOY HAVEN
card_summary: A multi-vendor toy marketplace with buyer, seller and admin roles. I built the Firebase backend, data model and security rules.
overview: Toy Haven is an online marketplace where independent shops sell toys and collectibles. Buyers browse and order, sellers manage their own shops, and admins manage accounts. I built the backend with Firebase.
features: Firestore data model for buyers, sellers and admins
Security rules so users can only change their own data
Sign-up and login with Firebase Auth, plus an admin panel that creates seller accounts and changes roles
Order workflow with stock checks and seller status updates
IndexedDB cache and HTTP caching rules for faster loading

highlight.sub: Homepage data load cut, 67.7 MB to 2.6 MB
highlight.text: Product photos were saved as text inside each product record, so every buyer downloaded every full-size photo. I moved the full photos to a separate collection and kept a small thumbnail on each product. Then I migrated all 135 products with no data loss.

title: PKMKPI PORTAL
card_summary: The national website for Filipino persons with disabilities, built by a volunteer team of 9 with accessibility first.
overview: PKMKPI is the national federation of persons with disabilities in the Philippines. Our volunteer team of 9 built its website. I built a full eight-page version, and it was one of five versions the project lead combined into the live portal.
features: 8 responsive pages in plain HTML and CSS, with no framework
Regions directory with island group filters, and the Disability Guide
Shared header, navigation and footer used on every page
WCAG contrast checks for visitors with low vision
Keyboard navigation, skip links and ARIA labels
Prototype accessibility panel (Alt+A) with text resizing, high contrast, a dyslexia-friendly mode and text-to-speech

title: THIS PORTFOLIO
card_summary: The site you are on. Plain HTML and Tailwind CSS, with a Node.js API that reads projects and saves contact messages in Supabase.
overview: My personal portfolio. The pages are plain HTML, Tailwind CSS and JavaScript with no framework. Behind them is a small Node.js API on Vercel that loads the projects from a Supabase database and handles the contact form.
features: 2 API routes on Vercel Functions: GET /api/projects and POST /api/contact
Projects load from Supabase, with a local JSON copy if the API cannot be reached
Contact form checked again on the server, with a hidden spam field and a limit of 3 messages per email every 10 minutes
Messages saved in Supabase and emailed to me with Nodemailer
Row Level Security on both tables, so only the server can read or write
Dark and light themes, a project popup with arrow-key slides, and links that open a project directly

decisions.q: Keep the database away from the browser
decisions.a: Both tables have Row Level Security with no public rules. Only the Node.js API, using the secret service key, can reach them.

decisions.q: Save the message before sending the email
decisions.a: If Gmail fails, the message is still saved and the visitor does not see an error.

decisions.q: Cache the projects list for 5 minutes
decisions.a: Vercel's CDN keeps a copy, so Supabase is not asked on every visit.
